html: The Cuttatawomen were two small Algonquian groups on the Rappahannock River in Virginia, one near its mouth on Chesapeake Bay and one further upstream. John Smith recorded both in 1608 as part of the wider chiefdom of Powhatan. Like their neighbours the Rappahannock, they lived by growing maize, fishing and hunting. After English settlers of the Virginia colony moved onto the river in the mid 1600s, they declined and merged into larger neighbouring groups, and they vanish from the records.
